notice.title: Mortgage arrears and forbearance
notice.aiSummary: Firms that lend or service residential mortgages must contact borrowers within 15 days of a missed payment and offer forbearance options before repossession. Compliance is required from February 1, 2027.
notice.aiReason: The notice applies to firms that lend or service residential mortgages, and Brivanta Bank originates and services residential mortgages.

text:
RETAIL CONDUCT AUTHORITY FICTIONAL REGULATOR - SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE
Final rule: Mortgage arrears and forbearance
Notice number: RCN-2026-020
Issued by: Retail Conduct Authority
Published: 2026-11-06
Effective date: 2027-02-01
1. Who this applies to
Firms that lend or service residential mortgages.
2. Background
Early contact gives borrowers in difficulty the best chance to recover.
3. Requirements
3.1 A firm must contact a mortgage borrower within 15 calendar days after a payment is missed.
3.2 A firm must offer a borrower in financial difficulty forbearance options, such as a temporary payment reduction, before starting repossession proceedings.
4. Status
Firms must comply with the requirements in section 3 from 2027-02-01.
Synthetic document written for a Snowflake example. The regulator, rule and numbers are fictional.

obligations.text: A firm must contact a mortgage borrower within 15 calendar days after a payment is missed.
obligations.controlDesc: Daily arrears report confirms contact attempts within 10 days of a missed payment
obligations.reason: Policy POL-MTG-01 requires contact within 10 calendar days, which is shorter than the 15 calendar days required by the obligation, and Control CTL-201 confirms these contact attempts within the same 10-day timeframe.

obligations.text: A firm must offer a borrower in financial difficulty forbearance options, such as a temporary payment reduction, before starting repossession proceedings.
obligations.controlDesc: Repossession checklist requires evidence that forbearance options were offered
obligations.reason: Policy POL-MTG-01 explicitly states "Borrowers in financial difficulty are offered forbearance options, including temporary payment reductions and term extensions, before any repossession proceedings start" and Control CTL-202 requires evidence that forbearance options were offered before repossession.
